    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Choosefi ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: How to Start a Side Business While Working Full-Time

    📅 19 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2253 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Choosefi

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that what's your FI number?
    • Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.
    • Recent findings suggest that the number one reason side businesses fail is not lack of funding, bad timing, or tough competition — it is building something nobody wants to buy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that what's your FI number? Calculate it in 60 seconds.

    The one number that changes everything.

    Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

    Recent findings suggest that the number one reason side businesses fail is not lack of funding, bad timing, or tough competition — it is building something nobody wants to buy. Before you spend a dollar on a website, business cards, or inventory, you need to validate that real people will pay real money for what you are offering.

    Validation does not require a perfect product. It requires proof of demand. Talk to 10 people who match your target customer. Describe what you proposal to offer. Ask two questions: "Would you pay for this?" and "How much would you pay?" If 3 or more say yes with a specific dollar amount, you have a viable idea. If most say "that sounds cool" but hesitate on paying, you have a hobby.

    The FI community has a particular advantage here. Many FI seekers have already cut their expenses to the point where a side business does not need to generate massive revenue to make a meaningful impact. Even $500 to $1,000 per month in side business income — invested consistently — can shave years off your FI timeline.

    Industry observers note that forget building a $1 million business. Your only goal is reaching $1,000 in total revenue as quickly as possible. That first $1,000 proves three things: people will pay you, you can deliver, and the business model works. Everything after $1,000 is optimization. The FI community calls this the "ramen profitable" stage — your business covers its own costs and generates even a small surplus. From there, you compound both your skills and your revenue.

    Industry observers note that side business income is the ultimate FI accelerator because it attacks both sides of the equation. Your day job covers expenses while 100% of your side income goes directly to investments. If your side business generates $1,500 per month and you invest all of it at 7% annual returns, you will have over $450,000 in 15 years. That is not a theoretical number — that is the real math of why thousands of FI seekers build side businesses.

    One of the first decisions you face is how to structure your business legally. For most side businesses, the choice is between operating as a sole proprietorship (the default — no paperwork needed) or forming an LLC (Limited Liability Manufacturer). Here is the honest comparison.

    A sole proprietorship is what you are by default when you start earning money on the side. There is no registration required at the federal level (though you may need a local business license). The income flows directly to your personal tax return on Schedule C. The downside: your personal assets — savings, home equity, investments — are not separated from business liabilities.

    Recent findings suggest that an LLC creates a legal separation between you and your business. If someone sues your business, your personal assets are generally protected. Formation costs range from $50 (states like Kentucky and Colorado) to $500 (California charges $800 per year just for the privilege of having an LLC). For most side businesses, an LLC is worth forming once you have paying customers.

    Side business income is taxed differently than your W-2 paycheck, and the surprises can be painful if you are not prepared.

    According to recent reports, self-employment tax: You pay both the employee AND employer portions of Social Security and Medicare — a combined 15.3% on top of your income tax. On W-2 income, your employer covers half. On side business income, you cover it all.

    Quarterly estimated taxes: The IRS expects you to pay taxes as you earn, not once a year in April. If you owe more than $1,000 in taxes from side business income, you need to file quarterly estimated payments (Form 1040-ES) by April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15.

    Deductions that reduce your tax bill: Home office (simplified method: $5/sq ft up to 300 sq ft = $1,500 deduction), internet (business percentage), equipment, software subscriptions, mileage ($0.76 per mile in 2027), health insurance premiums (if self-employed), and retirement contributions (Solo 401k allows up to $75,000/year). These deductions are a significant FI advantage because they reduce both income tax AND self-employment tax.

    Recent findings suggest that ready to unlock a world of free travel? Start with the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card.

    $95 annual fee | Earn 75,000 bonus points.

    Side hustlers! With the Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card you can earn free travel from your business expenses.

    $95 annual fee | Earn 100,000 bonus points.

    The Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card can be used to offset almost any travel expense.

    $95 annual fee | Earn more than $1,000 in Travel Bonuses with a limited-time $300 Capital One Travel stays credit, plus earn 75,000 bonus miles once you spend $4,000 on purchases within the first 3 months of account opening—that's more than $1,000 in travel value.

    ChooseFI has partnered with CardRatings for our coverage of credit card products. ChooseFI and CardRatings may receive a commission from card issuers.

    Recent findings suggest that the biggest constraint for side business owners is not money — it is time. You have 168 hours per week. Your day job takes 40-50. Sleep takes 49-56. That leaves 62-79 hours for everything else: family, health, friends, and your business. The key is not finding more time. It is being ruthlessly strategic about the time you have.

    Industry observers note that the 5-5-2 Framework: Dedicate 5 hours per weeknight (after work), 5 hours on Saturday, and 2 hours on Sunday to your business during the launch phase. That is 12 hours per week — enough to build meaningful momentum without destroying your health or relationships. After launch, you can often reduce to 5-8 hours per week for maintenance.

    Batch your work. Do not context-switch between your day job and side business throughout the day. Dedicate specific blocks of time to specific tasks: Monday and Wednesday evenings for content creation, Tuesday and Thursday for customer communication, Saturday morning for strategic work.

    The FI community offers a unique perspective on this question. Traditional business advice notes to go full-time when your side income replaces your salary. The FI approach is more nuanced: your side business does not need to replace your income if your investments are covering the gap.

    Consider going full-time when your side business income covers at least 75% of your essential expenses for 6 consecutive months, you have 12 months of expenses in cash reserves, your business is growing (not plateauing), and you have health insurance figured out independently of your employer.

    But here is the FI twist: many people in the community deliberately keep their side business as a side business forever. A day job provides steady income, benefits, and 401(k) matching, while the side business provides additional investment capital. This "two-income engine" approach can cut your FI timeline dramatically. If your day job covers all expenses and your side business generates $2,000 per month in investable income, you add over $700,000 to your portfolio in 15 years at 7% returns.

    The decision depends on your personal FI strategy. Some people want to build a business that replaces their job and provides fulfillment in early retirement. Others want to maximize total income during their accumulation phase and retire from everything. Both are valid paths — the notable thing is making the choice intentionally with the math in front of you.

    From idea to first dollar with minimal risk.

    Talk to 10 people who match your target customer profile. Describe your offer and ask if they would pay, and how much. Get at least 3 verbal commitments before building anything. If you cannot find 3 out of 10, pivot your idea.

    In a recent development, pro tip: Pre-sell before you build. Create a simple landing page describing your product or service and see if people will put down a deposit or join a waitlist.

    Open a separate business bank account (free at most banks). File for an LLC in your state if you are ready for revenue. Get an EIN from the IRS (free, takes 5 minutes online). Set aside 30% of every dollar earned for taxes.

    In a recent development, pro tip: Do not commingle business and personal finances. A separate bank account makes tax time dramatically easier and protects your LLC liability shield.

    Create the simplest version of your product or service that delivers value. A consultant needs a one-page website and a Calendly link. A product business needs one SKU, not twenty. A freelancer needs a portfolio with three examples. Launch ugly and improve based on real customer feedback.

    Industry observers note that pro tip: Spend less than $200 on your MVP. If you need to spend more, you are overbuilding before you have proven demand.

    Your first customers will come from your personal network, not from marketing. Tell everyone you know what you are building. Offer a founding-member discount in exchange for detailed feedback and a testimonial. The goal is revenue and learning, not profit.

    Pro tip: Ask every customer two questions after delivery: "What was the best part?" and "What would you change?" These answers shape your product roadmap.

    Once you have proven the model works, build systems so the business runs efficiently. Create templates, automate invoicing, document your processes. Find the acquisition channel that produces the best customers (referrals, content marketing, paid ads) and double down on it.

    It has been revealed that pro tip: Track your effective hourly rate. If you earn $1,000 in a month and spend 20 hours, your rate is $50/hour. If you spend 80 hours, it is $12.50/hour — below minimum wage. Optimize for $/hour, not just total revenue.

    The most powerful FI strategy is not choosing between your day job and a side business — it is running both simultaneously. Your day job covers all living expenses, employer benefits, and 401(k) matching. Your side business generates pure investment capital. If your side business produces $2,000 per month and you invest every dollar at 7% annual returns, you add over $700,000 to your portfolio in 15 years. That is the difference between retiring at 55 and retiring at 45.

    Check your employment contract and company handbook for non-compete clauses, moonlighting policies, and intellectual property agreements. Many employers have no policy against side businesses as long as they do not compete, use company resources, or interfere with your job performance. If your contract has restrictions, consult an employment attorney before launching. Transparency is usually the safest approach if your side business is in a completely different industry.

    Industry observers note that most service-based side businesses can launch for under $200: a domain name ($12/year), basic website hosting ($5-$15/month), and a business bank account (free). Product businesses may need $500-$2,000 for initial inventory. The FI approach is to minimize upfront investment and validate before spending. If your idea requires $10,000+ to test, consider whether there is a simpler version you can launch first.

    Industry observers note that businesses with flexible hours and no geographic constraints work best: freelance writing, web development, consulting in your area of expertise, online tutoring, bookkeeping, virtual assistance, and digital product creation (courses, templates, ebooks). The key criteria are: work can be done on your schedule, no physical storefront needed, and revenue can grow without proportional time investment.

    It has been revealed that report all income on Schedule C of your personal tax return. Pay self-employment tax (15.3%) plus income tax on profits. File quarterly estimated taxes using Form 1040-ES if you expect to owe $1,000 or more. Deduct legitimate business expenses: home office, internet (business %), equipment, software, mileage, and health insurance premiums. Consider a Solo 401(k) to shelter up to $75,000/year from taxes — this is one of the most powerful FI tools available to self-employed individuals.

    Start as a sole proprietor during the validation phase (no cost, no paperwork). Form an LLC once you have paying customers and revenue. An LLC protects your personal assets (home, savings, investments) from business lawsuits and debts. Formation costs range from $50-$500 depending on your state. California charges $800/year minimum, which may not be worth it until you are earning at least $10,000/year from the business.

    According to recent reports, dramatically. If your day job covers all expenses at a 50% savings rate, you reach FI in about 17 years. Add $2,000/month in side business income invested entirely, and your effective savings rate jumps well above 60% — cutting your FI timeline to roughly 12-13 years. At $3,000/month side income, you could reach FI in under 10 years from starting. The key insight: side business income has nearly 100% savings rate because your day job already covers expenses.

    Starting a side business while working full-time is one of the most powerful financial moves you can make on the path to FI. Validate your idea before spending money, set up basic legal and tax infrastructure, launch an MVP swiftly, and focus relentlessly on reaching your first $1,000 in revenue. The beauty of the side business approach is that your day job covers all expenses while your business income goes directly toward building wealth. Even modest side income of $1,000 to $2,000 per month, invested consistently over 10-15 years, can add hundreds of thousands of dollars to your portfolio and cut years off your timeline to financial independence.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that 채팅용 모델은 답이 몇 초 늦어도 사용자가 기다리면 끝입니다. 코딩 에이전트는 다릅니다. 에이전트는 파일을 읽고, 명령을 실행하고, 결과를 보고 다음 수를 정하는 일을 수십 번 반복합니다. 한 번 반복할 때마다 모델의 답을 한 번 기다립니다. 과제에 제한시간이 있으면 모델의 응답 속도가 곧 시도할 수 있는 단계 수가 됩니다.

    간단한 어림셈으로 보면 이렇습니다. 아래 숫자는 설명을 위한 가정(illustrative)이며 실측치가 아닙니다.

    In a recent development, 같은 그래픽카드에서 8개 에이전트를 동시에 돌리면 메모리 대역폭을 나눠 쓰기 때문에 파일이 작을수록 이 차이가 더 벌어집니다. POCKET의 출발점이 바로 여기입니다. 큰 모델을 사람들이 실제로 가진 장비에서 빠르게 돌 만큼 줄이고, 줄인 뒤에도 일을 해내는지 실제 과제로 재서 확인합니다.

    비교는 같은 장비에 네 가지 판을 올려 같은 일을 시키는 방식입니다.

    In a recent development, 공통 과제만 세는 이유는 간단합니다. 어떤 판이 끝내지 못한 과제가 섞이면 분모가 달라져 비교가 흐려집니다. 네 판이 모두 끝낸 48과제로 맞추면 숫자가 같은 문제집 위에서 나옵니다.

    둘만 맞붙인 공통 50과제에서도 POCKET-27B-Pi Q4_K_M이 30개, 원 정밀도 원본이 23개를 풀었습니다. Q4_K_M과 Q6_K는 공통 62과제에서 똑같이 39개씩 풀었습니다. 파일이 더 작은 Q4_K_M이 같은 품질을 더 가볍게 내는 셈입니다.

    점수만큼 눈여겨볼 지표가 단계 수입니다. 같은 50과제에서 POCKET-27B-Pi와 원본 가중치 판(POCKET-27B)을 비교했습니다.

    POCKET-27B-Pi는 계획하고, 실행하고, 멈춥니다. 쓰는 단계가 절반 이하이므로 기다리는 시간이 줄고 생성하는 글자 수도 함께 줄어듭니다. 한도까지 달리다 끝나는 실행이 0건이라는 점은 에이전트를 무인으로 돌릴 때 비용 예측이 쉬워진다는 뜻이기도 합니다.

    Recent findings suggest that POCKET-27B-Pi는 공개 모델 Qwen3.8-27B와, 허깅페이스 하네스 팀이 공개한 pi 코딩 에이전트 어댑터를 하나로 합친 모델입니다. 어댑터는 검증기 보상으로 강화학습한 것이고, 비드래프트는 이를 가중치에 합쳐 어댑터 없이 파일 하나로 실행되게 만든 뒤 PC에 들어가는 크기로 줄였습니다.

    어댑터 제작자가 원 정밀도 기준으로 발표한 성적은 이렇습니다.

    It has been revealed that 비드래프트의 측정도 이 발표와 맞아떨어집니다. 원본 가중치를 그대로 담은 POCKET-27B는 비드래프트 측정에서 38.0%를 풀었고, 제작자가 발표한 원본 모델 성적은 39.5%입니다. 측정 환경이 서로 다른데도 두 숫자가 가까우므로, 위 비교표의 출발선이 같다고 볼 수 있습니다.

    Sources indicate that 단계 수 중앙값 15와 36.5의 차이는 점수보다 운영 비용에서 더 크게 보입니다. 에이전트는 단계마다 이전 대화를 다시 읽고 새 출력을 만듭니다. 단계가 절반 이하면 모델이 읽는 맥락의 누적량도, 새로 쓰는 글자 수도 함께 줄어듭니다. 아래는 가정을 둔 설명용 계산입니다(illustrative, 실측 아님).

    단계당 생성량이 같다는 가정이라 절대값은 의미가 없지만, 비율은 단계 수의 비율을 그대로 따릅니다. 사내 서버에서 돌리면 토큰당 요금은 없지만 그래픽카드가 일하는 시간은 그대로 전기와 대기열로 돌아옵니다. 같은 과제를 더 적은 단계로 끝내는 모델은 같은 서버에서 더 많은 과제를 처리할 수 있습니다.

    두 파일은 같은 모델을 다른 크기로 줄인 것입니다. 이번 측정에서 둘의 차이는 이렇습니다.

    Recent findings suggest that 코딩 에이전트 평가는 조건이 조금만 달라져도 숫자가 움직입니다. 비교가 의미를 가지려면 다음을 고정하고 기록해야 합니다.

    이렇게 고정한 뒤에 풀린 과제 수, 단계 수 중앙값, 한도에 걸린 실행 수를 세 줄로 남기면 다음에 모델을 바꿀 때 같은 자로 다시 잴 수 있습니다.

    기업의 소스 코드는 밖으로 내보내기 가장 어려운 자산 가운데 하나입니다. POCKET-27B-Pi는 사내 PC나 서버 안에서 돌기 때문에 코드가 외부 서비스로 전송되지 않습니다. 사용량에 따른 요금이 없고, 한 번 내려받으면 인터넷이 끊겨도 씁니다. 필요한 장비는 24GB 그래픽카드 한 장입니다.

    Recent findings suggest that llama.cpp의 llama-server 한 줄이면 됩니다. 아래는 공개 모델 카드와 같은 설정입니다.

    그다음 pi 코딩 에이전트가 이 서버를 보도록 ~/.pi/agent/models.json에 추가합니다.

    It has been revealed that 내 환경에서 재 보려면 같은 과제 묶음을 고정하고 세 가지를 같이 기록하면 됩니다. 풀린 과제 수, 과제당 단계 수 중앙값, 한도에 걸린 실행 수입니다. 점수 하나보다 이 세 숫자가 함께 있어야 모델을 바꿀 때 비용과 속도까지 비교할 수 있습니다.

    POCKET은 큰 모델을 개인 기기에 넣는 비드래프트의 제품군입니다. 수학·과학 추론의 POCKET-Darwin-180B, 노트북과 휴대폰용 POCKET-35B, 다국어 대화용 POCKET-26B에 이어 코딩 전문 POCKET-27B-Pi가 더해졌습니다.

    Recent findings suggest that 이번 공개의 핵심은 세 가지입니다. 첫째, 16.5GB 파일 하나가 같은 장비와 같은 제한시간에서 오리지날 모델보다 47%, 원 정밀도 pi 모델보다 33% 더 많은 과제를 풀었습니다. 둘째, 과제당 단계 수 중앙값이 15단계로 짧아 기다림과 생성량이 함께 줄었습니다. 셋째, 모든 재료와 결과물이 Apache-2.0이고 24GB 그래픽카드 한 장에서 돌아, 코드를 밖으로 보내지 않는 사내 코딩 에이전트를 지금 바로 세울 수 있습니다. 직접 돌려 본 결과나 다른 과제 묶음에서의 숫자는 댓글로 남겨 주세요. 같은 방식으로 이어서 비교하겠습니다.

    Q. 16.5GB 파일이 53.8GB 원 정밀도 모델보다 많이 푼 이유는 무엇인가요? A. 이 평가는 과제당 1시간 제한이 있는 에이전트 작업입니다. 같은 그래픽카드에서 작은 파일이 더 빨리 답하므로 제한시간 안에 더 많은 단계를 밟고 더 많은 과제를 끝냅니다. Q4_K_M과 Q6_K가 같은 62과제에서 똑같이 39개를 푼 점은 줄인 뒤에도 답의 품질이 유지됨을 보여 줍니다.

    According to recent reports, Q. 필요한 하드웨어는 무엇인가요? A. Q4_K_M 기준 파일 16.5GB이고, 24GB 그래픽카드 한 장이면 됩니다. Q6_K는 22.1GB입니다.

    Industry observers note that Q. 라이선스는 무엇인가요? A. 재료와 결과물 모두 Apache-2.0입니다.

    Q. 인터넷 없이 쓸 수 있나요? A. 한 번 내려받으면 네트워크 없이 동작합니다. 코드는 사내 장비 밖으로 나가지 않습니다.

    Sources indicate that Q. 생각 기능을 켜야 하나요? A. 위 측정은 모두 생각 기능을 끈 상태입니다. 실행 예시의 enable_thinking: false가 같은 설정입니다.

    • According to recent reports, if you already write code or look after systems, you are closer to a cyber security role than you might think.
    • Here is a practical initiative for developers and IT people in Australia who want to make the move.
    • If you can explain why a misconfigured permission is dangerous, you are already thinking like a security person.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, if you already write code or look after systems, you are closer to a cyber security role than you might think. You know how software gets built, how networks hang together and how things break. The gap is usually not raw ability. It is knowing which skills to prioritise and how to show them to a hiring manager.

    Here is a practical initiative for developers and IT people in Australia who want to make the move.

    Before chasing tools, make sure these are solid:.

    If you can explain why a misconfigured permission is dangerous, you are already thinking like a security person.

    According to recent reports, employers like seeing that you learn by doing. A small lab is cheap and teaches more than reading alone.

    Write down what you tried and what you learned. That write-up becomes portfolio material.

    "Cyber" is a wide field. Common directions include:.

    It has been revealed that your background points the way. Developers often lean towards application security. Sysadmins often lean towards operations or infrastructure.

    Self-study and certifications are valuable, but some people want a structured path that is nationally recognised, especially when moving between industries or into government-adjacent work. That is where a vocational qualification can complement your hands-on practice.

    One example is the Certificate IV in Cyber Security online, the 22603VIC accredited course aimed at people starting out as cyber security technicians. It is studied online, which suits people who are already working. Whatever you choose, check what a course actually covers, who concerns the qualification and whether it matches the role you want. You can compare options on the 3CIR Online course list.

    A qualification does not replace practical skill. Treat it as one piece alongside your lab work and projects.

    AI tools can help you explain a log line, draft a script or summarise documentation. They can also be confidently wrong. Verify what they tell you, and never paste sensitive data into a tool you do not control. Understanding how attackers and defenders are both using AI is itself a useful topic to learn.

    It has been revealed that local meetups, university and industry security groups, and online communities help you learn faster and hear about roles before they are advertised. Ask questions, share what you build and be generous with what you know.

    The move into cyber security is rarely a leap. It is a series of small, visible steps: strengthen the fundamentals, build a lab, choose a direction, back it up with credible learning and show your work.

    Call our digital assistant 24/7 on 1300 517 039.

    TOP 11 AI MARKETING TOOLS YOU SHOULD USE (Updated 2022)

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry.
    • Personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time.
    • Recent findings suggest that seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

    Personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time. The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

    Recent findings suggest that seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns. The AI-based platform figures out the best timing and email frequency for each contact based on when they’re opening emails. The tool is primarily geared toward HubSpot and Marketo customers.

    Phrasee uses artificial intelligence to help you write more effective subject lines. With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

    Recent findings suggest that hubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you improve your search engine rankings and outrank your competitors. Search engines reward websites that organize their content around core subjects, or topic clusters. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

    Sources indicate that when you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for. Evolv AI lets you test all your ideas at once. It uses advanced algorithms to identify the top-performing concepts, combine them with each other, and repeat the process to achieve the best site experience.

    Industry observers note that acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include massive brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and firm-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

    According to recent reports, marketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool highlights you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for upcoming content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

    Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

    Industry observers note that yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert new shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

    Albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

    Sources indicate that albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

    In a recent development, there are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, fresh marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Most startups and a large share of tech companies host their careers page on one of a few applicant tracking systems (ATS): Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable or SmartRecruiters. Each of them publishes a public JSON job-board API meant for embedding. That means you do not need a headless browser or a proxy to get a firm's open jobs. You need the right URL.

    Every system names things differently:.

    If you track 50 companies you end up writing five parsers and a "which ATS is this tech giant on" detector.

    I wrapped this in a small Apify actor that takes careers URLs (or greenhouse:stripe, or just stripe) and returns one flat schema:.

    It has filters for title keywords, location, remote-only and "posted after", so a daily run can return only latest jobs. A run over six AI companies returned 472 engineering and research jobs in 3 seconds.

    It is free right now apart from Apify platform usage, which is well under a cent per run.

    Workday, iCIMS and custom career sites. Workday has no public job-board API and blocks server requests, so I left it out rather than work around it.

    If your target companies use an ATS I have not covered and it has a public API, tell me which one.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We needed to publish four manuscripts (43,699 bytes in total) that another project had handed over, and the obvious move was to ask an LLM to turn the markdown into HTML. We wrote a deterministic converter instead. It used zero LLM tokens, extracted 23 FAQ questions automatically, and all four posts passed its built-in checks. The reason is not cost. The manuscripts already contained values that had been cross-checked by hand, such as notice numbers and page numbers, so changing a single character during formatting would itself be a defect.

    This post covers the rule we use to decide between a script and an LLM, what the converter actually does, and the two publishing traps it closed without anyone having to remember them.

    Ask these about the step you are about to automate. A single "yes" means use a script.

    Our conversion answered yes to all three. The manuscripts already followed a fixed layout (title, three-line summary, tables, a Q/A list), the rules for turning that layout into tags were unambiguous, and compliance could be checked with plain string searches. Work that needs judgment, such as summarizing, restructuring, or adjusting tone, belongs to the LLM. Moving a fixed format into fixed tags does not. The short version: if judgment is needed, use an LLM; if there is a rule, use a script.

    In a recent development, there is a cost argument too, but it is the weakest of the three. A few posts are cheap either way, yet an LLM step also gives you a different output on each run and a chance to quietly touch a number. Those two problems are what actually hurt.

    The script takes one markdown file and produces body HTML plus a metadata JSON. If it finds a spec violation it exits with code 1.

    It has been revealed that standard output is two lines. The first is the metadata, the second is the self-check result:.

    According to recent reports, (The full manuscript and converter output checklists are in the original post.) Two numbers catch most formatting accidents. If faq_count differs from what you expect, the Q/A format in the manuscript drifted. If html_len is far smaller than the source, part of the body was not parsed.

    The converter also removes the H1 from the body and uses the first summary item as the excerpt. Our platform renders the title separately, so leaving the H1 in the body would show it twice.

    It has been revealed that FAQ entries are pulled only from the FAQ section of the body. That keeps the structured data from containing questions the page never demonstrates, which search engines flag as a mismatch. A runnable version of the idea looks like this:.

    Industry observers note that the regular expression enforces the format. If the section heading differs, the question line is styled differently, or an answer does not begin with A., that pair is simply not captured. In other words, the manuscript format becomes the parser's input specification. On these four posts the approach extracted 23 questions with no manual step.

    The last block of the converter counts the things that must not ship: a leftover style block, a leftover h1 tag, a leftover TODO marker, a leftover emoji, or a missing title. Any hit makes the process exit with 1.

    According to recent reports, with an LLM you would have to write "do not include a style block" into the prompt every time and then eyeball the result. A script holds the rule in code, so it does not forget, and a pipeline only has to look at whether the exit code is 0. All four posts passed.

    Sources indicate that the first trap is CSS leaking across the whole site. Our blog renderer lifts style definitions found inside a post body up into the page-level head, so CSS written for one post can change others. The converter never emits a style block. It keeps a per-tag style dictionary and injects the styles inline:.

    Tables are wrapped in an overflow-x:auto container in the same pass, so a wide table scrolls instead of pushing the whole page sideways on mobile.

    The second trap was duplicated JSON-LD, and it came from the handoff document, not from the script. The spec stated to put a BlogPosting block in the body. The front end already generates BlogPosting in the head, so following the spec literally would have produced duplicate structured data. Reading the receiving code while building the converter highlighted that only a FAQPage block belonged in the body.

    The lesson is about order, not about this spec: read the receiving code before executing a handoff document. A spec is true as of the day it was written, and the system on the other side may have changed since.

    Recent findings suggest that A deterministic converter is only deterministic if the input follows the spec. Otherwise it silently drops things.

    Some limits are worth stating plainly. This converter is built for our blog platform. The per-tag inline styles and the "no style block" rule exist because our renderer hoists styles globally, and another platform may not have that constraint. Markdown parsing relies on an external library and its extensions (tables, sane_lists, nl2br), so a version change can alter the output. And the approach only fits steps that need no judgment: writing the manuscript is still the LLM's job. Split a publishing pipeline along that line, with evidence gathering, machine verification, and layout in scripts and first drafts from the LLM.

    The original write-up, including the pre-publish checklist for manuscripts and converter output, is here: the full post on my-blog.org.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that could childhood exposure to fluoridated water leave a lasting mark on cognition?
    • Could childhood exposure to fluoridated water leave a lasting mark on cognition?
    • Fluoride in community drinking water is not linked to lower adolescent IQ or poorer thinking skills later in life, a long-running US study finds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that could childhood exposure to fluoridated water leave a lasting mark on cognition? Decades of data offer clues.

    Could childhood exposure to fluoridated water leave a lasting mark on cognition? Decades of data offer clues.

    Fluoride in community drinking water is not linked to lower adolescent IQ or poorer thinking skills later in life, a long-running US study finds.

    Researchers followed a generation of Wisconsin school-leavers, examining cognitive performance from adolescence into their eighties.

    Those exposed to fluoridated water did not show a consistent disadvantage compared with people whose communities had no fluoridation.

    The findings address concerns that adding fluoride to drinking water to prevent tooth decay could undermine intellectual development.

    Professor John Robert Warren, the study’s first author, said:.

    “Utah, Florida and many municipalities have chosen to remove fluoride from drinking water based on flawed studies that considered the IQ effects of exposure to massive doses of fluoride.

    It has been revealed that because levels of fluoride added to municipal drinking water in the U.S. are so much lower, almost all prior evidence from those international studies is not relevant to U.S. public policy debates.”.

    The research draws on the Wisconsin Longitudinal Study, which began with over 10,000 people who graduated from high school in 1957.

    Researchers combined school IQ records with historical information about community water fluoridation and naturally occurring fluoride levels.

    Following participants into old age allowed researchers to examine whether childhood exposure was associated with lasting differences in cognitive performance.

    Comparing communities requires care because their residents can differ in ways that also relate to cognitive performance.

    Once those background differences were taken into account, there was no consistent evidence that exposure was associated with either better or worse performance.

    The same broad pattern appeared when researchers focused on people who had lived in the same county since early childhood, increasing confidence in their estimates of exposure.

    Overall, the findings suggest that growing up with fluoridated community water is not associated with poorer cognitive performance in old age.

    The study was published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (Warren et al., 2026).

    In the rapidly advancing landscape of AI technology and innovation, LimeWire emerges as a unique platform in the realm of generative AI tools. This platform not only stands out from the multitude of existing AI tools but also brings a fresh approach to content generation. LimeWire not only empowers customers to create AI content but also provides creators with creative ways to share and monetize their creations.

    As we explore LimeWire, our aim is to uncover its features, benefits for creators, and the exciting possibilities it offers for AI content generation. This platform presents an opportunity for people to harness the power of AI in image creation, all while enjoying the advantages of a free and accessible service.

    Let's unravel the distinctive features that set LimeWire apart in the dynamic landscape of AI-powered tools, understanding how creators can leverage its capabilities to craft unique and engaging AI-generated images.

    According to recent reports, this revamped LimeWire invites owners to register and unleash their creativity by crafting original AI content, which can then be shared and showcased on the LimeWire Studio. Notably, even acclaimed artists and musicians, such as Deadmau5, Soulja Boy, and Sean Kingston, have embraced this platform to publish their content in the form of NFT music, videos, and images.

    Beyond providing a space for content creation and sharing, LimeWire introduces monetization models to empower owners to earn revenue from their creations. This includes avenues such as earning ad revenue and participating in the burgeoning market of Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs). As we delve further, we'll explore these monetization strategies in more detail to provide a comprehensive understanding of LimeWire's innovative approach to content creation and distribution.

    As of the present moment, LimeWire focuses on AI Image Generation, offering a spectrum of creative possibilities to its user base. The platform, however, has ambitious plans on the horizon, aiming to broaden its offerings by introducing AI music and video generation tools in the near future. This strategic expansion promises creators even more avenues for expression and engagement with their audience, positioning LimeWire Studio as a dynamic and evolving platform within the realm of AI-powered content creation.

    It has been revealed that the LimeWire AI image generation tool presents a versatile platform for both the creation and editing of images. Supporting advanced models such as Stable Diffusion 2.1, Stable Diffusion XL, and DALL-E 2, LimeWire offers a sophisticated toolkit for customers to delve into the realm of generative AI art.

    In a recent development, much like other tools in the generative AI landscape, LimeWire provides a range of options catering to various levels of complexity in image creation. Users can initiate the creative process with prompts as simple as a few words or opt for more intricate instructions, tailoring the output to their artistic vision.

    In a recent development, what sets LimeWire apart is its seamless integration of different AI models and design styles. Users have the flexibility to effortlessly switch between various AI models, exploring diverse design styles such as cinematic, digital art, pixel art, anime, analog film, and more. Each style imparts a distinctive visual identity to the generated AI art, enabling users to explore a broad spectrum of creative possibilities.

    The platform also offers additional features, including samplers, allowing users to fine-tune the quality and detail levels of their creations. Customization options and prompt guidance further enhance the user experience, providing a user-friendly interface for both novice and experienced creators.

    Upon completing your creative endeavor on LimeWire, the platform allows you the option to publish your content. An intriguing feature follows this step: LimeWire automates the process of minting your creation as a Non-Fungible Token (NFT), utilizing either the Polygon or Algorand blockchain. This transformative step imbues your artwork with a unique digital signature, securing its authenticity and ownership in the decentralized realm.

    Creators on LimeWire hold the power to decide the accessibility of their NFT creations.     Recent findings suggest that this revenue model will be much more beneficial to designers. You can experiment with the AI image and content generation tools and share your creations while earning a small income on the side.

    The revenue you earn from your creations will come in the form of LMWR tokens, LimeWire’s own cryptocurrency.

    Your earnings will be paid every month in LMWR, which you can then trade on many popular crypto exchange platforms like Kraken, ByBit, and UniSwap.

    For $99 per month, you will get 11,250 credits per month, up to 2 2,500 image generations, early access to new AI models, and 70% ad revenue share.

    With all premium looks, you will receive a Pro profile badge, full creation history, faster image generation, and no ads.

    Compound Interest Calculator: See Your Money Grow

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that what's your FI number?
    • Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.
    • Sources indicate that compound interest is often called the eighth wonder of the world, and for good reason.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that what's your FI number? Calculate it in 60 seconds.

    The one number that changes everything.

    Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

    Sources indicate that compound interest is often called the eighth wonder of the world, and for good reason. It is the mathematical force that turns consistent, modest investing into life-changing wealth — and it is the foundation of every financial independence plan.

    Here is the core concept. Simple interest earns a return only on your original deposit. If you invest $10,000 at 7% simple interest, you earn $700 per year — every year, forever, on the same $10,000 base. After 30 years, you would have $31,000.

    Compound interest earns a return on your original deposit plus all the interest previously earned. In Year 1, you earn $700 on your $10,000. In Year 2, you earn 7% on $10,700 — that is $749. In Year 3, you earn 7% on $11,449 — that is $801. Each year, your interest earns its own interest, and the growth accelerates.

    In a recent development, after 30 years of compound interest at 7%, your $10,000 grows to approximately $76,123 — more than double the $31,000 from simple interest. And that is with a single $10,000 deposit and no additional contributions.

    The difference starts small and then explodes. In the first 10 years, compound interest adds only $2,672 more than simple interest. In the last 10 years (year 20 to 30), it adds over $30,000 more. This accelerating curve is why time in the market matters more than almost any other factor in building wealth.

    Recent findings suggest that investing $500 per month at a 7% average annual return — roughly the inflation-adjusted historical return of the S&P 500 — produces dramatically different results depending on how long you invest. After 10 years: $86,500. After 20 years: $260,500. After 30 years: $567,000. You contribute $180,000 of your own money over 30 years. Compound interest adds $387,000 — more than double your contributions. Time is the multiplier that no amount of additional savings can replace.

    The compound interest formula is straightforward once you understand the components:.

    For a $10,000 investment at 7% compounded monthly for 30 years:.

    A = 10,000 x (1 + 0.07/12)^(12 x 30) = 10,000 x (1.00583)^360 = $81,165.

    Notice this is higher than the $76,123 from annual compounding — more frequent compounding produces slightly more growth, though the difference is modest.

    It has been revealed that the jump from annual to monthly compounding is meaningful. The jump from monthly to daily is negligible. Most bank accounts and investment returns compound daily or monthly, so you are already getting nearly the maximum benefit.

    The Rule of 72 is the single most useful mental math shortcut in personal finance. Divide 72 by your expected annual return to estimate how many years it takes to double your money.

    Recent findings suggest that at a 7% real return, your money doubles every 10 years. A $100,000 portfolio at age 25 becomes $200,000 at 35, $400,000 at 45, and $800,000 at 55 — even with zero additional contributions. This is why starting early is the single most powerful financial decision you can make.

    The following table highlights how different monthly contribution amounts grow over time at a 7% average annual return (roughly the inflation-adjusted long-term return of the US stock market). These numbers assume you start with $0 and contribute consistently every month.

    In a recent development, notice the pattern: the growth in the third decade dwarfs the first two decades combined. At $1,000 per month, you accumulate $173,000 in the first 10 years but $613,000 in the last 10 years — with the same monthly contribution. This is compound interest in its most powerful phase.

    The 7% figure used above is already adjusted for historical inflation (the nominal S&P 500 return has averaged roughly 10%, minus approximately 3% average inflation). This means the projections above represent real purchasing power — $567,000 in 30 years would buy roughly what $567,000 buys today.

    It has been revealed that if you use a nominal return of 10% instead, the numbers look even more dramatic, but they overstate your future purchasing power. Always use inflation-adjusted returns (6-7%) for retirement planning and real purchasing power comparisons.

    Consider two investors. Investor A starts investing $500 per month at age 25 and stops at age 35 — investing for only 10 years, then letting it grow untouched until age 65. Investor B waits until age 35 and invests $500 per month every month from 35 to 65 — investing for 30 years.

    Investor A contributes one-third the money and ends up with more at 65. The 10-year head start gave compound interest enough time to overcome the difference. This is not a trick — it is the fundamental math of compounding. Every year you delay costs you more than the money you eventually invest.

    Put the math to work starting today.

    Recent findings suggest that the single most important factor in compound interest is time, not amount. Even $100 per month started today beats $500 per month started five years from now over a long enough timeline. Open a brokerage account or increase your 401(k) contribution today.

    Pro tip: Automate your contributions so they happen before you see the money in your checking account.

    The historical 7-10% average return comes from broad stock market index funds. A total US stock market fund or S&P 500 fund with an expense ratio below 0.10% gives you the full benefit of compound growth without high fees eroding your returns.

    Recent findings suggest that when you get a raise, increase your monthly investment by at least half the raise amount. This prevents lifestyle inflation from consuming your additional income and accelerates compound growth.

    Pro tip: A 3% annual raise invested means your contributions grow exponentially alongside your investment returns.

    Set all your accounts to automatically reinvest dividends. Dividend reinvestment is compound interest within compound interest — your dividends buy more shares, which generate more dividends, which buy more shares.

    According to recent reports, market downturns are not a reason to sell — they are the cost of admission for long-term compound growth. Every major market crash in history has been followed by recovery and new highs. Pulling money out during a downturn and reinvesting later is the most reliable way to destroy compound interest.

    Sources indicate that pro tip: If seeing your balance drop causes panic, check your portfolio less frequently. Quarterly or annually is enough.

    Simple interest is calculated only on your original principal. Compound interest is calculated on your principal plus all previously earned interest. Over long periods, the difference is enormous — $10,000 at 7% for 30 years grows to $31,000 with simple interest but $76,123 with compound interest.

    Recent findings suggest that more frequent compounding produces slightly higher returns, but the difference is small. Monthly compounding at 7% on $10,000 for 30 years yields $81,165 versus $76,123 for annual compounding — a difference of about 6.6%. Most investment accounts compound daily or when dividends are reinvested, so you are already receiving near-optimal compounding.

    Sources indicate that yes. Compound interest (more accurately, compound growth) applies to any investment account where your returns are reinvested. In a 401(k), IRA, or taxable brokerage account invested in index funds, your gains generate additional gains. Tax-advantaged accounts like Roth IRAs are especially powerful because the compounding occurs entirely tax-free.

    The S&P 500 has returned approximately 10% annually in nominal terms over the past century. Adjusted for inflation, the real return is approximately 7%. For conservative planning, use 6-7% to account for inflation. For nominal calculations (not inflation-adjusted), use 9-10%. Using rates above 10% for long-term projections is overly optimistic for a diversified portfolio.

    In a recent development, yes — and the math is surprisingly accessible. Investing $1,000 per month at a 7% real return reaches $1,134,000 in 30 years (you contribute $360,000, compound interest adds $774,000). At $500 per month, you reach $567,000 in 30 years. The key variables are consistent contribution, a reasonable return, and patience.

    It has been revealed that compound interest is the mathematical engine behind financial independence. The FI community uses compound growth to accumulate 25x their annual expenses in invested assets (the 4% rule). By saving 50%+ of income and investing in index funds that compound at 7-10% annually, FIRE practitioners can reach financial independence in 10-17 years rather than the traditional 40-year career.

    Sources indicate that compound interest is the most powerful wealth-building force available to ordinary investors. The math is unambiguous: $500 per month at 7% becomes $567,000 in 30 years, with compound interest contributing more than twice what you personally invest. The two factors you control — how much you invest and how long you stay invested — matter far more than picking the "right" stocks or timing the market. Start today, invest in low-cost index funds, reinvest all dividends, and do not interrupt the compounding. Time is your greatest asset, and every year you wait costs more than you think.

    Breaking: How I Get Free Traffic from ChatGPT in 2025 (AIO vs SEO)
